paRequired.reason: Coded 'E' on the PDL because generic dabigatran is preferred at Tier 2; the document's own footnote states drugs coded 'E' may be excluded from coverage or subject to prior authorization specifically in Connecticut, New Jersey and New York -- Ohio is not one of those states, so brand Pradaxa is expected to be excluded from coverage outright rather than PA-eligible for a Ohio member, though the member's specific benefit plan should be confirmed.

Not listed anywhere in the UnitedHealthcare 2026 Commercial PDL (confirmed via full-text search of all 80 pages, including the alphabetical drug index) -- absent from the Anticoagulants section entirely, indicating it is not on this base formulary and would need a medical necessity/coverage exception request through Optum Rx rather than a stated PA pathway.

records.tier: Tier 2 ($$) -- UnitedHealthcare's mid-range-cost tier, per the PDL's own tier-cost definitions (p.4); no generic apixaban is listed on this PDL
records.verificationNote: Fetched the cited uhcprovider.com PDF directly via curl with a browser User-Agent (plain WebFetch is a known 403 risk for this domain per prior sessions' notes; curl got a clean 200 and a genuine 3.8MB PDF, confirmed with `file`). PDF metadata title reads 'Prescription Drug List - UnitedHealthcare Commercial Plans - Effective January 1, 2026' and the body's cover text reads '2026 Prescription Drug List', confirming the correct payer and effective date. Extracted full text with pypdf and read the 'Anticoagulants - Drugs to Treat or Prevent Blood Clots' section verbatim on page 11 of 80 (confirmed as the complete section: the table-of-contents page and the page-11 body both show the next class, Anticonvulsants, beginning immediately after it on the same page, so nothing was truncated). Confirmed line-by-line: dabigatran etexilate mesylate (generic) = Tier 2, QL; ELIQUIS TABLET = Tier 2, QL (no generic apixaban entry appears anywhere on the list -- confirmed by full-document search for 'apixaban', which returns zero other hits, and by the section itself starting alphabetically at 'dabigatran', meaning an 'apixaban' generic would sort before it if listed); rivaroxaban (generic) = Tier 2, QL; XARELTO (brand) = Tier 2, QL; warfarin sodium oral = Tier 1; jantoven (brand warfarin) = Tier 1; PRADAXA ORAL CAPSULE = coded 'E' (excluded from coverage / PA only in CT, NJ, NY per the legend on p.5), QL. Enoxaparin/LOVENOX entries were excluded from this record as out-of-scope (injectable LMWH, not an oral DOAC). Edoxaban/Savaysa does not appear anywhere in the document (confirmed via full-text search), so it is marked nonformulary. Since the source lists apixaban, rivaroxaban and dabigatran all at the identical Tier 2/QL/no-PA status with no single agent singled out as the top pick, apixaban/Eliquis was selected as the schema's single preferredAgent per this project's existing guideline-preferred-first-line-DOAC convention used across every other state's doac-anticoagulant class (e.g. ny-doac, pa-doac, ca-doac, ma-doac), not because the source itself names one brand over the others. The QL (quantity limit) flag present on every DOAC in this class is a dispensing-limit detail, not a PA/step barrier, so it is omitted from preferredRestriction per the task's instruction and noted here instead. No class-wide step-therapy criterion (e.g. a PA trigger for 2+ concurrent agents) appears anywhere in the Anticoagulants section or the front-matter program descriptions (pp. 4-6). [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]
